pre_intervention_diagnostic_item.context: Two identical bulbs in series with ammeters before, between, and after.
pre_intervention_diagnostic_item.distractor_revealing_misconception: Option A (A1 > A2 > A3 due to current consumption)

post_intervention_reassessment_item.stem: A circuit contains a 12V battery connected in series with a 100-ohm heating resistor R1 and a 20-ohm resistor R2. A technician measures the current entering R1 as I_in and the current leaving R2 as I_out. How do I_in and I_out compare?

options.text: I_in > I_out, because the 100-ohm resistor consumes more electric current than the 20-ohm resistor.
I_in = I_out, because in any series circuit, electric charge cannot accumulate or vanish, so the current flowing into the network must equal the current flowing out.
I_out > I_in, because the smaller resistor pushes current through faster.

post_intervention_reassessment_item.reassessment_diagnostic_rule: If student chooses A, the Current Attenuation misconception persists and requires secondary intervention with mechanical water circuit analog. If student chooses B, the misconception is marked resolved.

pre_intervention_diagnostic_item.context: Lower half of convex lens covered with black paper.
pre_intervention_diagnostic_item.distractor_revealing_misconception: Option A or B (top/bottom half of image disappears)

post_intervention_reassessment_item.stem: A concave mirror forms a clear image of a tree on a distant wall. A circular coin of radius 1 cm is taped directly over the central pole of the concave mirror, covering about 20% of its central reflecting area. What will be observed on the wall?

options.text: A circular black hole will appear in the center of the tree's image on the wall.
The entire image of the tree will remain complete and unbroken on the wall, but its brightness will be slightly reduced.
The tree's trunk will disappear, leaving only the leaves visible.

post_intervention_reassessment_item.reassessment_diagnostic_rule: Selecting A or C indicates persistence of the geometric blocking fallacy across optical reflections. Selecting B confirms generalized transfer to spherical mirrors.

pre_intervention_diagnostic_item.context: Stationary positive charge near magnetic poles.
pre_intervention_diagnostic_item.distractor_revealing_misconception: Option A or B (attractive/repulsive electrostatic force)

post_intervention_reassessment_item.stem: A stationary negative ion (Cl-) is held at rest right next to the North pole of a neodymium bar magnet in a vacuum chamber. What is the magnetic force acting on the ion?

options.text: A strong attractive force pulling the negative ion towards the North pole because North poles attract negative charges.
Zero, because static magnetic fields exert no force on stationary charges (v = 0).
A force perpendicular to the magnet pushing the ion out of the plane.

post_intervention_reassessment_item.reassessment_diagnostic_rule: Selecting A indicates persistent Pole = Charge equivalence. Selecting B verifies student distinguishes static electrostatics from velocity-dependent magnetic Lorentz interaction.
